q: Weihrauch reducibility classifies the computational difficulty of mathematical theorems by asking whether one theorem can be uniformly computably reduced to another. The Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT) is Weihrauch equivalent to:
opts: Connected choice: CC, the problem of finding a point in a non-empty connected closed set given its membership oracle
exp: IVT is Weihrauch equivalent to CC (connected choice on the reals): both have the same computational content. This places IVT in the Weihrauch lattice at the level of 'finding zeros of continuous functions'—computable but not computably uniform.
